title: Independent rate-backfill skip and failure diagnostic buffers

acceptanceCriteria.description: Six dimension skips retain five skip samples while a later thrown rate error remains visible in the independent failureSamples buffer.
Both diagnostic arrays survive the durable settings JSON write/read path, and legacy snapshots without skipSamples remain backward-compatible.
The backend classifies outcomes once, serializes both arrays, and the Rates and Orders DTOs pass them through without frontend or route reclassification.

Durable backfill crash, uncertain enqueue, restart, concurrency, and stale-generation fencing remain green, together with focused backfill regressions, strict TypeScript, and the production frontend build.
Verification is offline and non-mutating: no provider request, label purchase, postage charge, marketplace notification, production database write, or shipped/cancelled lifecycle change occurred.

canonicalOwners: src/services/rates-backfill.ts owns per-order skip/failure classification plus durable BackfillJobSnapshot serialization and settings reads
src/services/rate-backfill-diagnostics.ts owns the two independent five-entry buffers and backward-compatible diagnostic normalization
src/routes/rates.ts and src/routes/orders.ts are thin DTO pass-through consumers of backend-classified samples

oldOwners.path: src/services/rates-backfill.ts skip branches writing into the shared failureSamples capacity
oldOwners.delegatesTo: recordRateBackfillDiagnostic with explicit skip or failure classification

wrappers.delegatesTo: backend rate-job diagnostics as read-only DTO fields

sotBypass.details: Outcome classification, buffer capacity, serialization, and normalization remain backend-owned. Routes and clients only receive the two already-classified arrays.

evidence.proves: The exact PS-445 sequence records six dimension skips followed by one thrown error, retains the first five skips, preserves the real error independently, round-trips both arrays through durable JSON normalization, and defaults missing legacy skipSamples to an empty array.

PS-445 changes only the ticket-specific offline guard, command alias, and architecture evidence. The already-deployed canonical runtime split is present in the reviewed history, and no runtime, provider, order, shipment, label, migration, billing, or inventory file changed for this ticket.

migrations.rollbackPlan: No schema or data rollback is required. Forward-revert the PS-445 guard, package alias, documentation, and packet commits only; leave durable settings and historical diagnostic snapshots intact.

rollback.strategy: Forward-revert only the PS-445 ticket-specific proof and packet. The previously deployed independent diagnostic buffers remain safe and backward-compatible; do not rewrite durable settings, orders, shipments, or provider job history.

liveVerification.reason: The canonical runtime buffer split was already present in the deployed baseline, while PS-445 adds offline executable acceptance proof only. Live rate backfill would call carriers and write operational settings, so closure deliberately uses injected/static evidence and performs no provider or production mutation.
